_dividend_coverage_summary._finding: GAAP NII covered only ~91% of declared distributions over the trailing four quarters. Every one of the four quarters was short: the regular monthly dividend alone IS covered by NII, but the $0.30/quarter SUPPLEMENTAL is not. The gap is funded from realized gains and from the undistributed-taxable-income (spillover) buffer.

distributable_nii_non_gaap._definition: MAIN non-GAAP: GAAP NII excluding share-based comp and deferred comp expense.
distributable_nii_non_gaap._note: Even on MAIN's own more favourable non-GAAP DNII measure ($1.04), Q2 distributions of $1.08 were NOT covered. DNII-before-taxes ($1.08) exactly matches the distribution.

spillover_undistributed_taxable_income._finding: Distributions ($200.2mm) exceeded estimated taxable income ($162.1mm) by $38.2mm in the first half, drawing the spillover buffer down from $80.1mm carried in to $66.6mm carried out. Per share the buffer fell from $1.27 (6/30/25) to $0.71 (6/30/26) — a 44% decline in one year.
spillover_undistributed_taxable_income._source: Note G reconciliation of net increase in net assets to taxable income and total distributions declared

_dividend_coverage_summary.return_of_capital: NOT declared for the period. Note G states the tax character of distributions is determined ANNUALLY and interim estimates 'may not be representative'; it explicitly allows that distributions 'may also include either one or both of capital gains and return of capital'. Financial Highlights classify the full $2.16 6M distribution as 'Dividends paid from net investment income' on a TAX basis, which exceeds GAAP NII of $1.90 — the two measures are not the same and the difference is not reconciled per share.

risk_rating_migration._finding: NOT DISCLOSED. MAIN describes an 'internally developed investment rating system' for its LMM, Private Loan and Middle Market portfolio companies in both the 10-Q (Note B.4 and Item 2 MD&A) and the FY2025 10-K, but publishes NO numerical distribution of investments across rating buckets in either document — no counts, no fair-value-by-rating table, and therefore no migration.
risk_rating_migration.searched: Grepped both the Q2-2026 10-Q and the FY2025 10-K for 'investment rating', 'risk rating', 'Rating 1'..'Rating 5', and for any fair-value-by-rating table. Only qualitative descriptions of the methodology were found.
risk_rating_migration.closest_available_proxy: Non-accrual dollars/percentages at cost and fair value (disclosed quarterly) and the LMM/Private Loan strata cost-vs-fair-value split are the only quantitative credit-quality migration signals MAIN provides.
risk_rating_migration._comparability_flag: This is a REAL disclosure deficit relative to BDCs that publish rating-bucket tables. MAIN's premium to NAV is NOT accompanied by superior credit-quality disclosure granularity.

_top20_notes.ranking_basis: Fair value, aggregating ALL tranches of the same borrower into one position, from the Consolidated Schedule of Investments at June 30, 2026.
_top20_notes.borrower_names: VERBATIM as printed in the SOI, not normalized.
_top20_notes.CRITICAL_fv_pct_of_par_caveat: fv_pct_of_par is computed as TOTAL position fair value (debt + equity) divided by DEBT par, because MAIN co-invests equity alongside its loans in nearly every LMM position. It therefore routinely EXCEEDS 100% (up to 367% for OMi Topco) and is NOT a mark-integrity metric for MAIN and NOT comparable to a senior-loan BDC's FV/par. The _debt_only sub-object gives the apples-to-apples debt mark; use that for cross-manager comparison.
_top20_notes.debt_only_marks_top20: Debt tranches in the top 20 are marked at 98.0%-100.0% of par; 17 of the 20 are at exactly 100.0%.
_top20_notes.MSC_Adviser_I_LLC: Ranked #1 by fair value but is NOT a borrower — it is MAIN's wholly-owned External Investment Manager (see structural_notes). Retained in the ranking for completeness and flagged here; exclude it from any cross-manager borrower match.

internally_managed_structure._why_it_matters: MAIN is INTERNALLY managed: it pays NO base management fee and NO incentive fee to an external adviser. There is therefore NO incentive-fee mechanic keyed to NII at the MAIN level — the single largest structural difference from every externally managed BDC in the cohort, and a first-order explanation for a NAV premium that has nothing to do with mark quality.
internally_managed_structure._opex_note: Computed, not disclosed as a ratio: (compensation 14,239 + G&A 5,718 + share-based comp 5,807 - allocated to External Investment Manager 6,626) = 19,138 per quarter, annualized over total assets of $5,941,041K. Compare to a typical externally managed BDC's ~1.5% base management fee on gross assets PLUS a 17.5-20% incentive fee.

external_investment_manager.valuation_method: Waterfall valuation method under the market approach; Level 3. Change in fair value flows through 'Net Unrealized Appreciation (Depreciation) — Control investments'.

contribution_to_nii._composition: expenses allocated to the EIM plus dividend income earned from it

external_investment_manager.clients: MSC Income Fund (1.75% base management fee on average total assets, 17.5% subordinated incentive fee on income above a hurdle with 50%/50% catch-up, 17.5% incentive fee on cumulative net realized capital gains from 1/29/2025); MS Private Loan Fund I, LP; MS Private Loan Fund II, LP; other advisory clients.
external_investment_manager._FLAG: $225.2mm — 7.11% of net assets, $2.41 of the $33.92 NAV per share — is a Level 3 mark on MAIN's OWN captive asset-management business, against standalone book equity of just $29.5mm (itself an intangible). This is a marked-up internally-created asset with no third-party transaction reference. It was WRITTEN DOWN $29.8mm this half (from $255,020K at 12/31/2025 to $225,200K at 6/30/2026, -11.7%), the single largest negative mark move in the portfolio. Note the reflexivity: MAIN earns fees from MSC Income, a non-traded BDC it also advises.

portfolio_strata_split_at_fair_value._THE_KEY_FINDING: The consolidated 1.155x FV/cost is NOT a loan-mark premium. Decomposed: the LMM book (equity-heavy, 28.9% of cost in equity, 36% average fully diluted ownership) is marked at 1.258x cost, and the External Investment Manager at 7.63x cost. The PRIVATE LOAN book — the only stratum structurally comparable to a standard senior-loan BDC — is marked at 0.985x, i.e. BELOW cost. Portfolio-wide, debt tranches are marked at 96.5% of cost and 94.9% of par while equity is marked at 1.86x cost. MAIN's premium to NAV is an EQUITY-PARTICIPATION and CAPTIVE-ASSET-MANAGER story, not evidence that the market assigns higher integrity to its loan marks.

equity_participation_accounting._description: MAIN holds equity in ALL 94 of its LMM portfolio companies, averaging 36% fully diluted ownership. LMM equity is valued by an enterprise-value WATERFALL method (market approach using comparable private M&A multiples), while LMM/Private Loan debt is valued by a Yield-to-Maturity income approach. The waterfall method makes NAV directly sensitive to private-company EBITDA multiples rather than to credit spreads.

portfolio_wide_debt_vs_equity._source: Computed by the analyst from tranche-level SOI parsing, not disclosed as such by MAIN. Tranche-level roll-up totals $4,977,905K cost / $5,748,964K FV vs filing totals $4,974,649K / $5,746,044K — a +0.07% overstatement from tranche-row column irregularities. Company-level subtotals reconcile EXACTLY.

equity_participation_accounting.taxable_subsidiaries: Equity in pass-through portfolio companies is held through Taxable Subsidiaries (blocker corporations) to preserve RIC source-of-income compliance. These are consolidated for GAAP but NOT for tax, and generate a DEFERRED TAX LIABILITY of $124,258K at 6/30/2026 (up from $108,963K at 12/31/2025) — a real drag on realizable NAV that a pure senior-loan BDC does not carry. This DTL is 3.9% of net assets, or $1.33 per share.
equity_participation_accounting._note: The deferred tax liability means the $1,958,987K of equity appreciation is carried at a fair value against which a corporate-level tax will be owed on realization. NAV is stated net of this DTL.

fair_value_hierarchy._note: 99.59% of the portfolio is Level 3 (significant unobservable inputs). Only $23.4mm (0.41%) has a quoted price. There is effectively NO market-observable validation of MAIN's marks.

leverage_detail._note: Shares outstanding on the balance sheet (93,354,166) differ slightly from the Financial Highlights figure (93,359,325); the highlights figure is used for per-share spillover and EIM-per-share calculations.

market_value_at_period_end._source: Note F Financial Highlights, 'Market value as of the end of the period'
market_value_at_period_end._note: This is the filing's OWN primary-source price/NAV at 2026-06-30: 1.529x. Any higher current multiple reflects price movement after the balance-sheet date, not a different NAV.

structural_notes.incentive_fee_mechanics_keyed_to_nii: NONE at the MAIN level (internally managed). The only incentive-fee mechanics in MAIN's disclosure run the OTHER way: MAIN's subsidiary EARNS a 17.5% subordinated incentive fee on income above a hurdle from MSC Income Fund and its private funds. MAIN is a fee RECIPIENT, not a fee payer.

coverage_gaps: QUARTERLY PIK DOLLARS NOT DISCLOSED. PIK is quantified only as a six-month cash-flow reconciliation line ('Payment-in-kind interest'). The requested current-quarter vs year-ago-quarter comparison is therefore substituted with six-month vs six-month. Searched: 'PIK', 'payment-in-kind', 'payment in kind' across the full 10-Q; the investment-income note and MD&A disaggregate by interest/dividend/fee and by control classification but never by cash vs PIK.

INTERNAL RISK RATING DISTRIBUTION NOT DISCLOSED in either the Q2-2026 10-Q or the FY2025 10-K. The rating system is described qualitatively only; no bucket counts, no fair value by rating, hence no migration. Searched both documents for 'investment rating', 'risk rating', 'Rating 1'-'Rating 5' and any by-rating table.

NON-ACCRUAL COMPANY COUNT (17) IS DERIVED, not stated. MAIN discloses only dollars and percentages. The count was obtained by counting distinct companies bearing SOI footnote (14); the derived cost/FV roll-up ($198,593K / $65,323K) reconciles to the disclosed $198.5mm / $65.2mm, which validates the method.
PRIOR-YEAR NON-ACCRUAL DOLLARS NOT DISCLOSED. The 6/30/2025 10-Q gives percentages only (2.1% at FV, 5.0% at cost), so a year-ago dollar comparison is unavailable from primary source.

Q4 2025 NII PER SHARE AND DISTRIBUTIONS ARE DERIVED BY SUBTRACTION (FY2025 10-K minus 9M2025 10-Q). MAIN does not publish a standalone Q4 income statement. Q4 weighted-average share count is itself derived from FY vs 9M weighted averages, so the $1.03 Q4 NII/share carries approximation risk of roughly +/-$0.01.
NAV PER SHARE AT 3/31/2026 IS DERIVED (net assets / shares from the Statements of Changes in Net Assets = $33.4586). The 10-Q states NAV/share only at 6/30/2026 and 12/31/2025.

COST BY STRATUM IS DISCLOSED ONLY FOR LMM AND PRIVATE LOAN (in millions, one decimal). Cost for Middle Market, Other Portfolio and the External Investment Manager strata is not given in the strata table; only fair value is. Strata FV/cost for those three could not be computed.

TRANCHE-LEVEL PARSE CARRIES +0.07% NOISE. Analyst-computed tranche roll-up ($4,977,905K cost / $5,748,964K FV) exceeds filing totals ($4,974,649K / $5,746,044K) by ~$3.3mm because 41 of 210 company blocks have tranche rows with irregular column layouts. All company-level cost/FV figures reported here use the filing's own subtotal rows and reconcile EXACTLY to the filing totals. Only the debt-vs-equity split and the par figures carry this noise.

'PAR' FOR EQUITY POSITIONS IS NULL BY CONSTRUCTION. MAIN's SOI reports Shares/Units in the same column position as Principal for equity tranches; par and fv_pct_of_par are therefore null for pure-equity positions and debt-only par is used where a position blends debt and equity.

TAX CHARACTER OF DISTRIBUTIONS IS AN INTERIM ESTIMATE. Note G explicitly states the determination is made annually and that an interim determination 'may not be representative'. Whether any portion of the trailing-four-quarter $4.29 is return of capital cannot be established from this filing.

MAIN DOES NOT DISCLOSE A WEIGHTED-AVERAGE INTERNAL LEVERAGE OR LOAN-TO-VALUE FIGURE for its portfolio companies, nor portfolio-company-level EBITDA leverage multiples. Only average EBITDA ($11.8mm LMM / $39.3mm Private Loan) is given, so the attachment point of MAIN's debt cannot be assessed from primary source.
